summary: Adds a novel top-level command `garmin-pp-cli sql <query>` (internal/cli/garmin_sql.go, internal/cli/garmin_sql_test.go), registered on the root command beside `insights` with one AddCommand line and a comment at internal/cli/root.go, and lifts the MCP sql tool's statement gate into a new hand-owned package internal/sqlguard so the command and the tool enforce one contract. WHY THE PRESS CANNOT EXPRESS THIS: the press emits `sql` only as an MCP tool (internal/mcp/tools.go registers it with handleSQL); there is no generated CLI verb, and the two generated CLI read paths over the archive are `analytics` (count or group one resource type by one top-level JSON field) and `search` (FTS5 text match). Neither can express an arbitrary aggregate, a join across two series, or json_extract on a nested path. WHAT IT DOES: runs exactly one SELECT or WITH...SELECT against the local archive, read-only, with no network call on any path. Output goes through the same helpers the generated commands use (wantsHumanTable, printJSONFiltered), so --json, --agent, --compact, --csv, --plain, --quiet and --select behave identically to every generated command; a TTY gets the tab-separated table in the query's own column order. --db defaults through garminArchivePath, the same resolver `insights` and `history` use, so --home and GARMIN_HOME are honoured. Deadline and row budget are the MCP tool's own bound.WithSQLQueryDeadline and bound.NewSQLScanState (SQLMaxRows 10000, MaxBytes 60000); a bounded result sets truncated:true, the cap that actually stopped the scan (max_bytes, or max_rows when the row backstop is what fired) and note in the envelope rather than silently returning a short answer. The envelope is this command's own shape, not a field-for-field mirror of the MCP tool's, which carries store_status, resumable and returned_count instead. TWO LAYERS, NEITHER TRUSTED ALONE: (1) internal/sqlguard.Validate refuses anything that is not a single SELECT or WITH statement, after stripping the leading whitespace, line comments, block comments and semicolons SQLite itself skips — so `-- x\nDROP TABLE resources`, `/* x */ DROP ...` and `SELECT 1; ATTACH ...` are refused, not just bare DROP. (2) The handle is opened mode=ro with _pragma=query_only(true), so the CTE-wrapped write the gate deliberately does not parse (`WITH x AS (...) INSERT ...`) answers SQLITE_READONLY. ONE DISCLOSED SIDE EFFECT, AND IT IS NOT THE QUERY'S: resolving the default --db goes through garminArchivePath, the resolver `insights` and `history` share, which pins a data.db in a home that has none and renames a single token-scoped archive to the home's name; the store's own open then migrates that file, so a run in a fresh home leaves a migrated but empty archive behind — measured at 196608 bytes with 0 rows and no garmin_series_state, the same footprint `insights` leaves — and the read-only open then creates the usual -shm and an empty -wal beside it. That happens before the query runs, is the same behaviour every archive-reading command has, and is skipped entirely by --db. No archived row is changed on any path. Both layers are load-bearing and each is proved separately by test: mode=ro alone does NOT stop `ATTACH DATABASE` from creating a file (measured on modernc.org/sqlite v1.37.0, this build), and a prefix-only keyword check does not stop a leading comment. WAL: the handle deliberately omits immutable=1. store.OpenReadOnlyContext carried immutable=1 until N131.5.5 (see garmin-store-readonly-wal.json), so the two DSNs differed; they are now the same shape. On a WAL fixture with a writer connection open, mode=ro&immutable=1 was measured to report `no such table` for a table that exists and to miss a committed row that had not been checkpointed; plain mode=ro sees it. TestGarminSQLSeesUncheckpointedWALCommit asserts both halves so the difference stays attributable to the flag.
reason: N131 decision D20 (owner, 2026-09-13): `insights` answers the two questions we knew to ask, and the largest benefit is in the questions we did not — an archive of years of daily series has no fixed recipe list. `sql` is the escape hatch that makes the archive worth filling for a question nobody anticipated, in the same 'Local state that compounds' group as `history`. It is hand-written rather than adapted from the espn CLI's `sql` verb because that verb's prefix-only keyword guard over a read-write handle was demonstrated to pass a CTE INSERT, REPLACE, ATTACH and VACUUM INTO (owner memory, 2026-08-22); that is the exact failure this build's two layers prevent, case by case, in TestGarminSQLBlastRadius.
generated_files_edited: internal/mcp/tools.go — validateReadOnlyQuery, stripLeadingSQLNoise and hasTrailingSQLStatement (lines 927-1075 of the ae88a370b file) are replaced by three delegating bodies at lines 928-949, plus one import line for internal/sqlguard in the import block. The function names and signatures are unchanged, so the generated tests in internal/mcp/tools_test.go that call them directly still compile and still pass.
internal/cli/root.go — one rootCmd.AddCommand(newGarminSQLCmd(flags)) plus a six-line comment, beside the existing insights registration.
validated_outcome: go build ./... exit 0, go vet ./... exit 0, gofmt -l clean, go test -count=1 ./... green with 0 FAIL. TestGarminSQLBlastRadius runs eleven statements through the verb against a WAL fixture and sha256s the database file before and after each: a CTE INSERT, REPLACE, ATTACH, VACUUM INTO a scratch path, PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE, `SELECT 1; DROP TABLE resources`, a line-comment-hidden DROP, a block-comment-hidden DROP, writefile() and load_extension() are each refused with the bytes unchanged and no file created in the scratch directory; a plain SELECT returns its two rows. TestGarminSQLHandleRefusesWritesWithoutTheGate re-runs the write forms straight against the handle, bypassing the gate entirely, and asserts PRAGMA query_only is 1. TestGarminSQLRefusesAFlagAfterTheQuery pins the other silent shape: a flag written after the bare -- used to be joined onto the query as a SQL line comment, so the query ran and the flag was dropped at exit 0; it is now refused by name. TestMCPSQLGuardIsTheSharedGuard asserts handleSQL refuses with byte-identical wording to sqlguard.Validate, which is the only thing that catches a re-render silently un-sharing the gate. Empty and missing archives: a store with no rows answers zero rows at exit 0 with a stderr hint naming `garmin-pp-cli history --since all`, and an archive that has rows but no match for the query gets a different next_step naming the filter instead. LIVE: run against the owner archive with GARMIN_HOME unset (~/.local/share/garmin-pp-cli/data.db, 2022 rows across 15 resource types at the time of the run) — a resource_type census, a json_extract grouped by month over the activities series, and a join of the activities and activity_hr_zones series on the id they share all returned rows.
regen_notes: A re-render of internal/mcp/tools.go restores validateReadOnlyQuery, stripLeadingSQLNoise and hasTrailingSQLStatement inline and drops the internal/sqlguard import. That compiles and the CLI verb keeps working, so nothing fails loudly except internal/mcp/sql_shared_guard_test.go, which is the reason that file exists. Re-apply the three delegating bodies and the import after any dogfood/generate run, then run that test.

The command is registered AFTER the typed MCP sql tool in cmd/garmin-pp-mcp, so cobratree's walker sees s.GetTool("sql") != nil and skips the name rather than shadowing the typed tool (internal/mcp/cobratree/walker.go). A regen that reorders registration, or that stops emitting the typed sql tool, would turn `sql` into a shell-out mirror with a different contract. internal/mcp/tools_test.go already asserts the typed description survives; keep that assertion.

`sql` shares garminArchivePath, insightsSyncCommand, isMissingArchive and formatInsightValue with internal/cli/garmin_sync.go and internal/cli/garmin_insights.go. Those files are one novel unit: restoring this one without them does not compile.

The table list in the command's Long help is asserted against a freshly migrated store by TestGarminSQLHelpTablesExist, including garmin_series_state, which the windowed walk creates rather than the generated migration. A regen that renames a store table fails that test rather than shipping help that names a table the binary does not create.

FIXED IN N131.5.5 ROUND 2 (was: OPEN, NOT FIXED HERE) — store.OpenReadOnlyContext (internal/store/store.go) opened mode=ro&immutable=1, and openMCPReadOnlyStore (internal/mcp/tools.go) backs BOTH the MCP `sql` and `search` tools with it. On a WAL fixture with a writer connection open, that handle missed a committed row and reported `no such table` for a table that exists. immutable=1 is now dropped and query_only(true) added, so the store's DSN matches this command's; the change, its measured read-only-directory cost and the two generated tests it repaired are recorded in .printing-press-patches/garmin-store-readonly-wal.json.

The table list in the Long help says garmin_series_state is created by the first history run. A fresh home's migrated archive does not have it (measured this build), which is why TestGarminSQLHelpTablesExist calls EnsureGarminSeriesState before checking the list.
